## IMF quota data

I'm going to start by reading in my IMF quota data, which I already did last week, and then I will start to go through the steps to clean it.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate)
library(tinytable)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
# Reading in raw quota data

raw_quota_data <-
  read.csv("raw_quota_data.csv")

head(raw_quota_data)
```

```{r}
# Trying to drop columns

quota_data <- 
  select(raw_quota_data, 1, 2)

# Trying to drop the rows that are not the actual variables

quota_data <-
  slice(quota_data, 3:195)

# Renaming columns

quota_data <-
  rename(quota_data,
         country_name = Table.1..Updated.Quota.Formula.Variables.Shares.1.,
         quota_percent = X)

# Arranging in alphabetical order (to make it easier to merge eventually)

quota_data <-
  arrange(quota_data, country_name)

# Renaming China instead of China 2/ (which indicates that it includes some Chinese territories) to be the same as in the other dataset

quota_data <-
  quota_data |>
  mutate(
    country_name = str_replace_all(country_name, "China 2/", "China")
  )
  
quota_data
```

I still need to run some tests to make sure these numbers make sense - mostly just want to make sure they add up to 100.

## IMF conditionality data

Now I'm going to start with cleaning my IMF conditionality data. This will be more complicated because I'll first need to clean it as it is, and then I'll need to create a new data frame with counts of each condition, as opposed to listing each condition. I was going to keep in the condition text just in case I decide to run some sort of analysis on that, but it seems like only those that are unusual are coded in that way so I'm gonna remove it.

I think actually I'm just gonna keep country name and condition type, plus condition policy area for if I need it later (I think I might).

```{r}
# Reading in raw conditionality data

raw_conditionality_data <-
  read.csv("raw_IMF_conditionality_data.csv")

raw_conditionality_data 
```

```{r}

  select(raw_conditionality_data, 1, 8, 13)
```

### Cleaning the conditionality data now that I have the right kinds of data frames (for now)

Now I need to change the variable names of df_type_original and df_policy_area, as well as for total_conditionality. After that I'll try to mutate the tables so I can combine them all together. I think missing variables will really give me a headache but hopefully it works.

I'm going to start by putting my three different data frames in the same code chunk. Then I'll change the variable names one at a time, and then I'll go from there.

```{r}
# First, putting my three data frames in

head(df_type_original)

head(df_policy_area_original)

head(total_conditionality)

# Trying to make them into tibble

df_type <- 
  as_tibble(as.data.frame.matrix(df_type_original), rownames = "country_name")

df_type

df_policy_area <- 
  as_tibble(as.data.frame.matrix(df_policy_area_original), rownames = "country_name")

df_policy_area

total_conditionality <-
  as_tibble(total_conditionality)

total_conditionality

# THIS WORKED! 

# Now I want to change the variable names to be more readable

# I'm going to do that in a new chunk in case I fuck it up

```

Now I'm going to try to slowly but surely and very carefully merge the data frames on conditionality. I'll try to merge with the other data set later.

```{r}
# First, going to try to merge the conditionality data frames

merged_conditionality <-
  bind_cols(total_conditionality, df_type, df_policy_area)

# Ok this made the issue of including the country name 3 times, so I'll have to drop two

merged_conditionality <-
  select(merged_conditionality, 1:2, 4:9, 11:18)

# The only issue left is that country_name got messed up

merged_conditionality <-
  rename(merged_conditionality,
         country_name = "country_name...1")

merged_conditionality
  
```

Merged the conditionality data set! Now I need to merge that with my quota data. (Which will not be fun).
